lessons.title: Transport
lessons.scenario: Smarty shows Mia and Sam different ways to travel in his garage.

items.example: The red train is big.
items.note: Say ‘train’ for a long vehicle that runs on tracks.

image.describe: a bright red train on tracks with Smarty the black cat waving from a window

items.example: I like this white plane.
items.note: Use ‘plane’ for a vehicle with wings that flies.

image.describe: a sleek white and blue airplane flying above fluffy clouds with a happy cat pilot

items.example: The blue boat is on the water.
items.note: Say ‘boat’ for a vehicle that travels on water.

image.describe: a small blue wooden boat floating on calm water with Smarty the black cat wearing a captain hat

items.example: His new motorbike is yellow.
items.note: Use ‘motorbike’ for a bike with a motor that goes fast.

image.describe: a shiny yellow motorbike parked outside a garage with a cat helmet on the seat

items.example: My new suitcase is under the table.
items.note: Say ‘suitcase’ for a large bag you use when you travel.

image.describe: a brown suitcase with brass buckles sitting next to a cat paw print

grammar.title: by train, by plane, by boat
grammar.explanation: Use ‘by’ before a way to travel, with no ‘a’ or ‘the’: by train, by plane, by boat, by motorbike.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a vehicle on tracks. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A train runs on tracks.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a flying vehicle with wings. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A plane flies in the air.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: The blue boat is on the water.
practice.answer: The blue boat is on the water.
options: The blue boat is on the water.
The blue train is on the water.
The big suitcase is on the table.
practice.explanation: A boat travels on the water.

practice.prompt: Match each phrase with the matching way to travel.
practice.explanation: Use ‘by’ before train, plane, boat, or bus.

practice.prompt: Sam cannot ride a bike, but he has a yellow ___. Complete the sentence.
practice.text: He cannot ride a bike, but he has a ___.
practice.explanation: A motorbike is a bike with a motor.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about where the suitcase is.
practice.answer: My green suitcase is under the bed.
practice.explanation: Put the subject ‘My green suitcase’ first, then ‘is under the bed’.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about going to England.
practice.text: We go to England ___ plane.
practice.explanation: Say ‘by plane’ with no ‘a’ or ‘the’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I like the red train and the blue boat.
practice.answer: I like the red train and the blue boat.
practice.explanation: Great job saying ‘train’ and ‘boat’ clearly.

story.hook: What does Smarty have in the garage?

image.describe: Inside Smarty's cozy garage: Smarty the black cat stands beside a shiny yellow motorbike, a red model train, a white toy plane, a small blue boat, and a big brown suitcase while Mia and Sam look around happily.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Mia! Hello, Sam! This is my new motorbike.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: It is yellow! And what is that?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: That is my small blue boat.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I see a red train and a white plane too!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Is this big brown suitcase yours, Smarty?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes, it is mine! I love planes, trains, and boats.

questions.prompt: What colour is Smarty’s motorbike?
questions.explanation: Mia says: It is yellow!

questions.prompt: What is big and brown?
questions.explanation: Mia asks: Is this big brown suitcase yours, Smarty?

mission.setup: Smarty asks how you like to go to new places. Answer in your own words.

turns.smarty: I like trains and planes! Do you like trains?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say if you like trains.

turns.smarty: How do you go to school or work? By bus, by train, or by motorbike?
turns.hint: Say by train, by bus, by car, or by motorbike.

turns.smarty: I have a big brown suitcase. What colour is your suitcase?
turns.hint: Name a colour, like blue or black.

lessons.title: January to May
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Ana look at a big wall calendar in the garage.

items.example: January is cold in England.
items.note: Say ‘January’ for the first month of the year; always start it with a capital letter.

items.example: It is cold in February.
items.note: Use ‘February’ for the second month of the year.

items.example: Spring is in March.
items.note: Say ‘March’ for the third month, when spring often begins.

items.example: It is rainy in April.
items.note: Use ‘April’ for the fourth month of the year.

items.example: Every tree is green in May.
items.note: Say ‘May’ for the fifth month, when the weather is warm.

grammar.title: in January, in May
grammar.explanation: Use ‘in’ before a month, and always write months with a capital letter: in January, in March, in May.

practice.prompt: Which month comes first in the year?
practice.explanation: January is month number one.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: February is the second month and is often cold.

practice.prompt: Match each number with its month.
practice.explanation: January is one, February is two, March is three, April is four, and May is five.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about spring.
practice.text: Spring is in ___.
practice.explanation: Spring starts in March.

practice.prompt: Choose the right word before a month.
practice.text: It is rainy ___ April.
practice.explanation: Use ‘in’ before months: in April.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about the weather in May.
practice.answer: It is warm and sunny in May.
practice.explanation: Put ‘in May’ at the end of the sentence.

practice.prompt: Say the first five months aloud.
practice.text: January, February, March, April, May.
practice.explanation: Well done saying the first five months in order.

story.hook: Which month does Ana like best?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Ana stand in the garage looking at a colorful picture calendar showing snow for winter and blossoms for spring, with no written words.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What is the weather like in January, Ana?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: In January and February, it is cold.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Do you like March and April?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes! In March, spring is here. In April, it is rainy.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And do you like May?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I love May! It is warm and sunny, and every tree is green.

questions.prompt: What is the weather like in January and February?
questions.explanation: Ana says: In January and February, it is cold.

questions.prompt: Which month does Ana love?
questions.explanation: Ana says: I love May!

mission.setup: Smarty asks about the weather in the first five months where you live.

turns.smarty: In my home, January is cold. Is it cold in January where you are?
turns.example: Yes, it is cold in January.
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say what the weather is like in January.

turns.smarty: March, April, May! Which one is your favourite?
turns.hint: Say January, February, March, April, or May.

lessons.title: June to October
lessons.scenario: Ben and Smarty talk about summer and autumn in the garage.

items.example: Summer is in June.
items.note: Say ‘June’ for the sixth month, when summer starts.

items.example: It is hot and sunny in July.
items.note: Use ‘July’ for the seventh month, often the hottest time of summer.

items.example: We swim every day in August.
items.note: Say ‘August’ for the eighth month of the year.

items.example: We go to school in September.
items.note: Use ‘September’ for the ninth month, when school starts again.

items.example: It is windy in October.
items.note: Say ‘October’ for the tenth month, in the middle of autumn.

grammar.title: Seasons and months
grammar.explanation: Pair ‘in’ with both seasons and months: in summer, in July, in autumn, in October.

practice.prompt: Which month comes right after May?
practice.explanation: May is month five, and June is month six.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: It is hot and sunny in July.
practice.answer: It is hot and sunny in July.
options: It is hot and sunny in July.
It is cold and rainy in April.
practice.explanation: July is a hot, sunny summer month.

practice.prompt: Match each number with its month.
practice.explanation: June is six, July is seven, August is eight, September is nine, and October is ten.

practice.prompt: Complete the summer months.
practice.text: Summer is June, July, and ___.
practice.explanation: August is the eighth month, right after July.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about school.
practice.text: We go to school in ___.
practice.explanation: School starts in September.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about autumn.
practice.answer: Autumn is in September and October.
practice.explanation: September and October are autumn months.

practice.prompt: Say the months from June to October aloud.
practice.text: June, July, August, September, October.
practice.explanation: Nice job saying months six through ten.

story.hook: When does Ben go to school again?

image.describe: In the garage, Ben holds a basketball while talking to Smarty the black cat near an open window showing sunny summer trees outside.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Summer is here, Ben! Do you like June and July?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes! In June and July, it is hot. I swim and play basketball.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What do you do in August?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: In August, we have a picnic in the park.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And in September and October?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: In September, I go to school. In October, it is windy and cloudy.

questions.prompt: What does Ben do in August?
questions.answer: He has a picnic in the park.
options: He has a picnic in the park.
questions.explanation: Ben says: In August, we have a picnic in the park.

questions.prompt: When does Ben go to school?
questions.explanation: Ben says: In September, I go to school.

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your summer and autumn months.

turns.smarty: I love July and August! What do you do in summer?
accept: ^i (?:swim|play football|play tennis|play basketball|read|sleep|have a picnic)(?: in (?:june|july|august|summer))?$
turns.hint: Tell Smarty one thing you do in June, July, or August.

turns.smarty: In September and October, it is autumn. Do you like autumn?
turns.hint: Say Yes or No, or say if you like September or October.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Leo sort travel gear and plan seasons in the garage.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence with the right travel item.
practice.explanation: You carry your things in a suitcase when you travel.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: She is on the red train.
practice.answer: She is on the red train.
options: She is on the red train.
She is on the blue boat.
She is on the yellow motorbike.
practice.explanation: Listen for ‘red train’ at the end.

practice.prompt: Match each month with its number.
practice.explanation: January is one, March is three, June is six, and October is ten.

practice.prompt: Fill in the missing month.
practice.text: January, ___, March, April.
practice.explanation: February comes between January and March.

practice.prompt: Fill in the missing month.
practice.text: August, ___, October.
practice.explanation: September comes between August and October.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: We go by boat in August.
practice.explanation: Use ‘by boat’ for transport and ‘in August’ for the month.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: England is far. We go by ___.
practice.explanation: A plane takes you far places quickly.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: In May and June, it is warm and sunny.
practice.answer: In May and June, it is warm and sunny.
practice.explanation: Great pronunciation of May and June.

story.hook: How do Smarty and Leo go to England in July?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat and Leo sit beside a big blue suitcase in the garage, looking at a white model plane and a map.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Smarty, England is far! Do we go by train?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, Leo. We go by plane in July.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: What is the weather like in England in July?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: In July and August, it is warm and sunny.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I have a big blue suitcase. Is it good?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! Now we have a suitcase and a map.

questions.prompt: How do Smarty and Leo go to England?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: We go by plane in July.

questions.prompt: When do they go to England?
questions.explanation: Smarty says they go in July.

mission.setup: Smarty checks what you remember from Lessons 1 to 3.

turns.smarty: Name one way to go far: plane, train, boat, or motorbike!
turns.hint: Say plane, train, boat, or motorbike.

turns.smarty: Which month do you like: January, May, July, or October?
turns.hint: Say a month from January to October.

lessons.title: My birthday
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Zara celebrate a birthday in the garage.

items.example: It is cold and rainy in November.
items.note: Say ‘November’ for the eleventh month of the year.

items.example: Winter is in December.
items.note: Use ‘December’ for the twelfth and last month of the year.

items.example: January is a cold month.
items.note: Say ‘month’ for one part of the year; more than one is ‘months’.

items.example: There are twelve months in one year.
items.note: Use ‘year’ for all twelve months from January to December.

items.example: My birthday is in November.
items.note: Say ‘birthday’ for the special day each year when you were born.

image.describe: a festive birthday cake with glowing candles, balloons, and Smarty the black cat wearing a party hat

grammar.title: When is your birthday?
grammar.explanation: Ask ‘When is your birthday?’ and answer with ‘in’ plus the month: ‘My birthday is in December.’

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a cake and party hat. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: We celebrate a birthday every year.

practice.prompt: Which month is the last month of the year?
practice.explanation: December is month number twelve.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for ‘November’ at the end.

practice.prompt: Match the pairs.
practice.explanation: November is eleven, December is twelve, and twelve months make one year.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: August is a warm ___.
practice.explanation: August is one month of the year.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: There are twelve months in one ___.
practice.explanation: One year has twelve months.

practice.prompt: Ask Smarty about his birthday.
practice.explanation: Start the question with ‘When is’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: My birthday is in December.
practice.explanation: Remember to use ‘in’ before December.

image.describe: In the garage, Smarty the black cat brings a sweet chocolate cake with candles to Zara, who smiles beside a winter snow globe.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Zara, when is your birthday?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: My birthday is in December. It is in winter!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And when is his birthday?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: His birthday is in November. We love cake!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: There are twelve months in a year, and two birthdays here!

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: Thank you, Smarty! This cake is delicious.

questions.prompt: When is Zara’s birthday?
questions.explanation: Zara says: My birthday is in December.

questions.prompt: How many months are in a year?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: There are twelve months in a year.

mission.setup: Smarty wants to know when your birthday is.

turns.smarty: My birthday is in May! When is your birthday?
turns.hint: Say: My birthday is in… and your month.

turns.smarty: How many months are there in one year?
accept: ^(?:there are )?twelve(?: months)?(?: in one year| in a year)?$

lessons.title: I'm going to visit
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Tom talk about their plans for tomorrow and next week in the garage.

items.example: I am going to read a book.
items.note: Use ‘I am going to’ plus an action word to talk about your plans.

items.example: I am going to play football tomorrow.
items.note: Say ‘tomorrow’ for the day after today.

items.example: We are going to go to the museum next week.
items.note: Use ‘next week’ for the seven days after this week.

items.example: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
items.note: Say ‘visit’ when you go to see a person or a place.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat knocking happily on the front door of a cozy cottage where a grandmother cat waves hello

items.example: Where are you going next week?
items.note: Ask ‘Where are you going?’ to find out someone’s destination.

grammar.title: going to + action
grammar.explanation: Use ‘am / is / are going to’ before a base verb to talk about future plans: I am going to visit, she is going to swim, we are going to read.
examples: I am going to visit my aunt.
He is going to play tennis tomorrow.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of Smarty at his grandmother’s door. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: You visit a person or a place when you go to see them.

practice.prompt: Yesterday was Monday. Today is Tuesday. Wednesday is ___.
practice.explanation: Tomorrow is the day after today.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: ‘Where are you going?’ asks about someone’s plan.

practice.prompt: Match the beginnings and endings of these plans.
practice.explanation: Pair ‘going to’ with an action word like visit, swim, or go.

practice.prompt: Complete the plan with the right word.
practice.text: I ___ going to visit the museum.
practice.explanation: With ‘I’, use ‘am’: I am going to.

practice.prompt: Complete the time phrase.
practice.text: They are going to go to England ___ week.
practice.explanation: Say ‘next week’ for the week after this one.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about tomorrow’s plan.
practice.answer: I am going to visit my friend tomorrow.
practice.explanation: Put ‘I am going to visit’ first, then ‘my friend tomorrow’.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.answer: Where are you going next week?
practice.explanation: Ask ‘Where are you going’ before ‘next week’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I am going to visit my uncle next week.
practice.answer: I am going to visit my uncle next week.
practice.explanation: Smooth work using ‘going to’ and ‘next week’.

story.hook: Where is Tom going next week?

image.describe: In the garage, Smarty the black cat points at a map on a table while Tom holds a red model train.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello, Tom! Where are you going tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Tomorrow I am going to visit my grandfather.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Are you going to go by bus?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: No, I am going to go by train.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And where are you going next week?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Next week I am going to visit Uzbekistan!

questions.prompt: Who is Tom going to visit tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Tom says: Tomorrow I am going to visit my grandfather.

questions.prompt: Where is Tom going next week?
questions.explanation: Tom says: Next week I am going to visit Uzbekistan!

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your plans for tomorrow and next week.

turns.smarty: Tomorrow I am going to read a book. Where are you going tomorrow?
accept: ^i am going to (?:swim|read|sleep|play football|play tennis|play basketball|study|cook)$
turns.example: I am going to visit my friend.
turns.hint: Start with: I am going to…

turns.smarty: And what are you going to do next week?
accept: ^(?:next week )?i am going to (?:visit|go to|swim|read|play football|play tennis|play basketball|study|walk|run)(?: (?:my )?(?:england|brazil|uzbekistan|friend|grandmother|grandfather|park|museum|school))?(?: next week)?$
turns.example: I am going to visit England next week.
turns.hint: Say: I am going to… next week.

lessons.title: Packing
lessons.canDo: Say what you need and want for a trip
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia pack a suitcase in the garage.

items.example: I am going to pack my suitcase tomorrow.
items.note: Say ‘pack’ when you put things into your suitcase or bag.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat neatly folding a red T-shirt and placing shoes into an open suitcase

items.example: I need my toothbrush and my shoes.
items.note: Use ‘need’ for things you must have.

items.example: I want to pack my blue jacket.
items.note: Say ‘I want to’ before an action word to talk about something you would like to do.

items.example: You need a passport on a plane.
items.note: Say ‘passport’ for the small book you show when you go to another country.

image.describe: a dark blue passport booklet with a gold globe emblem resting on a wooden table

items.example: I want to pack my new camera.
items.note: Use ‘camera’ for the device you use to take pictures.

image.describe: a black and silver digital camera with a strap lying next to a yellow hat

grammar.title: need + thing vs. want to + action
grammar.explanation: Put a noun after ‘need’ (I need my passport) and an action word after ‘want to’ (I want to pack my camera).
examples: I want to pack my camera.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a small blue travel booklet. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: You need a passport when you fly to another country.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a device for taking photos. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A camera takes pictures.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I am going to pack my suitcase.
practice.answer: I am going to pack my suitcase.
options: I am going to pack my suitcase.
I am going to visit my aunt.
I want to ride a bike.
practice.explanation: You pack your suitcase before you go away.

practice.prompt: Match the sentence halves.
practice.explanation: Use ‘need’ with a thing, and ‘want to’ or ‘going to’ with an action.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: It is rainy in England. I ___ my umbrella.
practice.explanation: Use ‘need’ for something you must have in the rain.

practice.prompt: Complete the phrase before the action ‘pack’.
practice.text: I want ___ pack my yellow T-shirt.
practice.explanation: Say ‘want to’ before an action word like ‘pack’.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I need my passport and my map.
practice.explanation: Put ‘I need’ before the two things you must have.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I want to pack my new camera.
practice.explanation: Use ‘I want to pack’ before ‘my new camera’.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I need my passport and I want to pack my camera.
practice.answer: I need my passport and I want to pack my camera.
practice.explanation: Great contrast between ‘need’ and ‘want to’.

image.describe: In the garage, Smarty the black cat and Mia kneel beside an open brown suitcase filled with a jacket, shoes, a camera, and an umbrella while a blue passport sits on a wooden table.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Smarty, we are going to go by plane tomorrow!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! I am going to pack my big suitcase now.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: What do you need?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I need my jacket, my toothbrush, and my umbrella.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I want to pack my camera too!

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: My passport is on the table! I need my passport!

questions.prompt: What does Mia want to pack?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I want to pack my camera too!

questions.prompt: Where is Smarty’s passport?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: My passport is on the table!

mission.setup: You are packing a suitcase with Smarty. Tell him what you need and what you want to pack.

turns.smarty: We are going to go by plane! What do you need?
turns.hint: Say: I need my passport (or suitcase, camera, umbrella).

turns.smarty: Good! And what do you want to pack in your suitcase?
turns.example: I want to pack my camera.
turns.hint: Start with: I want to pack my…

lessons.title: The big trip
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Sam are ready to leave from the garage for their big trip.

items.example: You are going to visit Brazil tomorrow. Have a good trip!
items.note: Say ‘Have a good trip!’ to wish someone a safe and happy journey.

items.example: I bought a beautiful postcard at the museum.
items.note: Say ‘postcard’ for a picture card you buy and mail when you are away.

image.describe: a colorful illustrated postcard showing a sunny mountain and a tiny airplane, with no written words

items.example: Our hotel is near the park.
items.note: Use ‘hotel’ for a place where you pay to sleep when you visit another town.

image.describe: a welcoming multi-story yellow hotel building with balconies, flower boxes, and a cat bellhop at the door

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a building where travelers sleep. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: A hotel is a place where you sleep on a trip.

practice.prompt: Look at the picture of a holiday picture card. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: You buy a postcard to share pictures from a trip.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Say ‘Have a good trip!’ when someone goes away.

practice.prompt: Match each action with the right word.
practice.explanation: You sleep in a hotel, fly by plane, pack a suitcase, and buy a postcard.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.text: Our ___ is big and clean.
practice.explanation: A hotel is a building with clean rooms.

practice.prompt: Complete the plan for next week.
practice.text: Next week we ___ going to visit Brazil.
practice.explanation: With ‘we’, use ‘are’: we are going to.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about the last month of the year.
practice.text: My birthday is in ___, the last month of the year.
practice.explanation: December is the twelfth and last month of the year.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I need my passport for my trip.
practice.explanation: Put ‘I need my passport’ before ‘for my trip’.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: I want to buy a beautiful postcard.
practice.explanation: Use ‘I want to buy’ before ‘a beautiful postcard’.

practice.prompt: Say the lines aloud.
practice.text: Have a good trip! Buy a postcard at the hotel.
practice.answer: Have a good trip! Buy a postcard at the hotel.
practice.explanation: Great job using all three new expressions together.

story.hook: Where are Smarty and Sam going for their big trip?

image.describe: Outside the open garage door, Smarty the black cat and Sam stand with their packed suitcases and a camera while Mia waves goodbye.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Where are you going, Smarty and Sam?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: We are going to visit Brazil in August!

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Do you have your passports and your suitcases?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes! I packed my camera too. I want to buy a postcard for you.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Our hotel is near the park. It is big and yellow.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Have a good trip! See you in September!

questions.prompt: Where is Smarty and Sam’s hotel?
questions.explanation: Sam says: Our hotel is near the park.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty want to buy for Mia?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I want to buy a postcard for you.

questions.prompt: What does Mia say at the end?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Have a good trip!

mission.setup: Plan a full trip with Smarty! Answer his questions in your own words.

turns.smarty: Let's plan a trip! Where are you going?
accept: ^i am going to (?:visit |go to )?(?:england|brazil|uzbekistan|the park|the museum|my grandmother|my grandfather|my friend)$
turns.example: I am going to visit Brazil.
turns.hint: Say: I am going to visit England (or Brazil, Uzbekistan).

turns.smarty: When are you going, and how? By plane or by train?
turns.hint: Say a month or next week, and by plane or by train.

turns.smarty: What do you need in your suitcase?
turns.example: I need my passport and my camera.
turns.hint: Say: I need my passport (or camera, jacket).

turns.smarty: You are going to sleep in a nice hotel! Say goodbye to me!
accept: ^(?:goodbye|bye|see you later)(?: smarty)?(?: have a good trip)?$
turns.example: Goodbye, Smarty! Have a good trip!
turns.hint: Say Goodbye or Have a good trip!

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Tomorrow is August! Sam and I are going to visit Brazil.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat stands excitedly in the garage next to a wall calendar and a bright globe.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: We have two big suitcases, a camera, and a map.

image.describe: Sam holds up a camera and a folded map beside two packed suitcases in the garage.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Our plane is at nine o'clock in the morning.

image.describe: A wall clock in the garage points to nine o'clock while a toy white plane sits on a shelf.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: You are going to sleep in a yellow hotel near the park. Have a good trip!

image.describe: Mia smiles and waves at Smarty and Sam near the open garage door.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Thank you, Mia! I am going to buy a beautiful postcard for you.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat gives a cheerful thumbs-up with his paw.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Smarty, where is your passport? Is it in your suitcase?

image.describe: Sam looks worried as he checks inside an open brown suitcase in the garage.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: No! My passport is not in my suitcase, and it is not on the table! Where is it?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat looks surprised with wide eyes, searching around an empty table in the garage while tiny paw prints lead toward the door.
